+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import collections.abc as cabc
+import typing as t
+from contextlib import contextmanager
+
+from .exceptions import BadParameter
+from .exceptions import UsageError
+
+if t.TYPE_CHECKING:
+    from .core import Context
+    from .core import Parameter
+
+
+@contextmanager
+def current_usage_context(
+    ctx: Context, param: Parameter | None = None
+) -> cabc.Iterator[None]:
+    """Context manager that attaches extra information to exceptions.
+
+    Works like :func:`click.core.augment_usage_errors`, except the given
+    ``ctx`` always replaces any context already set on the error. This
+    attributes errors to the current invocation, for example when a
+    command forwards to another command.
+    """
+    try:
+        yield
+    except BadParameter as e:
+        e.ctx = ctx
+        if param is not None and e.param is None:
+            e.param = param
+        raise
+    except UsageError as e:
+        e.ctx = ctx
+        raise
diff --git a/tests/test_current_usage_context.py b/tests/test_current_usage_context.py

+++ b/tests/test_current_usage_context.py
@@ -0,0 +1,76 @@
+import pytest
+
+import click
+from click.current_usage_context import current_usage_context
+
+
+def test_attaches_ctx_when_missing():
+    ctx = click.Context(click.Command("cmd"))
+
+    with pytest.raises(click.UsageError) as exc_info:
+        with current_usage_context(ctx):
+            raise click.UsageError("bad")
+
+    assert exc_info.value.ctx is ctx
+
+
+def test_replaces_existing_ctx():
+    inner = click.Context(click.Command("inner"))
+    outer = click.Context(click.Command("outer"))
+
+    with pytest.raises(click.UsageError) as exc_info:
+        with current_usage_context(outer):
+            raise click.UsageError("bad", ctx=inner)
+
+    assert exc_info.value.ctx is outer
+
+
+def test_bad_parameter_replaces_ctx_and_keeps_param():
+    inner = click.Context(click.Command("inner"))
+    outer = click.Context(click.Command("outer"))
+    existing = click.Option(["--a"])
+    other = click.Option(["--b"])
+
+    with pytest.raises(click.BadParameter) as exc_info:
+        with current_usage_context(outer, other):
+            raise click.BadParameter("bad", ctx=inner, param=existing)
+
+    assert exc_info.value.ctx is outer
+    assert exc_info.value.param is existing
+
+
+def test_bad_parameter_sets_missing_param():
+    ctx = click.Context(click.Command("cmd"))
+    param = click.Option(["--a"])
+
+    with pytest.raises(click.BadParameter) as exc_info:
+        with current_usage_context(ctx, param):
+            raise click.BadParameter("bad")
+
+    assert exc_info.value.param is param
+
+
+def test_bad_parameter_without_param():
+    ctx = click.Context(click.Command("cmd"))
+
+    with pytest.raises(click.BadParameter) as exc_info:
+        with current_usage_context(ctx):
+            raise click.BadParameter("bad")
+
+    assert exc_info.value.ctx is ctx
+    assert exc_info.value.param is None
+
+
+def test_other_exceptions_pass_through():
+    ctx = click.Context(click.Command("cmd"))
+
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
+        with current_usage_context(ctx):
+            raise ValueError("bad")
+
+
+def test_no_error():
+    ctx = click.Context(click.Command("cmd"))
+
+    with current_usage_context(ctx):
+        pass
notes:
Added current_usage_context as a contextmanager mirroring augment_usage_errors but unconditionally setting e.ctx on BadParameter/UsageError (param still only filled when missing); types imported under TYPE_CHECKING to avoid a circular import with core. Added unit tests in tests/test_current_usage_context.py.
